notes: Net map (4 nodes): n1 = top rail -- upper lead of V-DC 0 (47kV) up to the corner (127,185), then right along y~185, T-tapped at (211,185) by the top lead of inductor 3 (57mH), and on into the LEFT terminal of I-DC 2 (49A) at x~281. n2 = RIGHT terminal of I-DC 2 across to the LEFT plate of capacitor 1 (60uF) at x~356. n3 = RIGHT plate of capacitor 1 (x~367) right to the corner (449,196), down the right side to (449,264) and left along y~262 into the RIGHT end of resistor 4 (54ohm). 0 = ground -- lower lead of V-DC 0 down to (124,304), right along the bottom wire at y~304, T-joined at (210,304) by the bottom lead of inductor 3, continuing right to the vertical at x~269; that vertical runs from the LEFT end of resistor 4 at (269,255) down through the bottom wire to the GND 5 plate at (269,322). Judgment calls: (a) this drawing is in faint pencil and most of the long wires are rendered as broken/dashed runs of pixels after binarisation (the top rail, the bottom wire, the capacitor-to-right-side lead and the bottom of the right loop are all dashed). Every one of those gaps was checked at 7-8x: the segments are collinear, evenly spaced and end-to-end with no symbol between them, so they are single continuous wires, not breaks. Reading any of them as a break would strand a component. (b) The junction where the bottom wire meets the resistor-4/GND vertical at (269,305) is a clean T (the vertical is continuous from y=255 to y=317 and the horizontal arrives from the left and stops), so resistor 4's left end, the GND, the V-DC lower lead and the inductor's lower lead are one node. (c) There are no wire crossings anywhere in this drawing, so no dot-vs-hop calls. (d) I-DC 2's arrow points right; terminal 0 is its left lead. V-DC 0 and inductor 3 are vertical, terminal 0 = top; capacitor 1 and resistor 4 are horizontal, terminal 0 = left. (e) The long thin lines at x~5, y~140 (upper right) and y~365 (lower left) are page/scan-border artefacts and touch no component.
